 Mauricio Pochettino is due to take charge of US games on Saturday and Wednesday Photograph: Harry How/Fifa/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino is due to take charge of US games on Saturday and Wednesday Photograph: Harry How/Fifa/Getty Images Manchester United Manchester United close on Mauricio Pochettino deal before settling Carrick’s fate 
 Pochettino wants to leave USA role for United
 United board meeting scheduled for Wednesday
 Jamie Jackson Wed 11 Nov 2026 03.56 EST Last modified on Wed 11 Nov 2026 04.51 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Manchester United are closing in on agreeing a deal for Mauricio Pochettino to become their head coach if Michael Carrick is sacked in line with the recommendation from Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.
 Pochettino is the US men’s national team head coach but wants the United job if, as expected, Carrick is removed.
 Firing a manager is often more about maintaining the illusion of control | Leander Schaerlaeckens Read more Wilcox and Berrada are meeting Ratcliffe in Monaco, where the minority owner will be informed that Carrick should lose his job. Ratcliffe controls United’s sporting policy.
 There is a growing sense among United players that Carrick will be sacked, with their expectation being that Pochettino will replace him. Pochettino has managed in the Premier League with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.
 A United board meeting is scheduled for Wednesday at which one or more of the six Glazer siblings who are the majority owners will be represented. There is an expectation within the executive and in Carrick’s camp that the sacking will be ratified there and that an announcement will follow.
 Pochettino’s contract contains a release clause of about $10m (£7.5m), although the compensation United would have to pay will be higher if the Argentinian brings his own staff, including his longtime assistant and confidant Jesús Pérez, who has worked with Pochettino for 16 years.
 Pochettino is due to take charge of the US in Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday in Miami and Cincinnati respectively, their first competitive fixtures of the 2030 World Cup qualifying cycle.

 Carrick has overseen a disastrous start to their season which has United in 18th and in the relegation zone. The 45-year-old has won only one game in the league, against Ipswich in August, and three in all competitions. United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton in September.
